市場の量り売りからネット通販まで。値段を聞く、まけてもらう、スマホで払う。中国の: From buying produce by weight at the market to online shopping. Asking prices, getting a discount, paying by phone: shopping in China is more fun than you think.
果物屋さんで量り売り: Buying fruit by weight at a fruit stand
杭州の大学に留学して一か月の鈴木くん。寮の近くの小さな果物屋さんは、いつも地元の: Suzuki has been studying at a university in Hangzhou for a month. The little fruit stand near his dorm is always busy with locals. Today he's going to try buying something on his own for the first time. As he looks at the apples piled high out front, the owner, Zhao, calls out to him cheerfully.
寮の近くの果物屋の店主、四十代。声が大きくておしゃべり好き、常連さんにはすぐおま: Owner of a fruit stand near the dorm, in her forties. Loud and chatty; quick to throw in something extra for regulars
杭州に留学中の日本人大学生、二十一歳。中国語は日本で一年勉強した: Japanese university student studying in Hangzhou, 21. Studied Chinese for a year in Japan
近所のお店の店主とお客さん。中国の個人商店はとても距離が近く、店主は初対面でも「: A neighborhood shopkeeper and a customer. Small independent shops in China are very friendly, and the owner will cheerfully call you 「小伙子」 ("young man") even the first time you meet. For the customer, starting with 「你好」 and doing a little light bargaining is just right for the relationship.
お兄さん、何にする？: Young man, what can I get you?
「小伙子」は若い男性への気さくな呼びかけ。お店では「帅哥」（イケメン）、女性なら: 「小伙子」 is a friendly way to address a young man. In shops you may also be called 「帅哥」 ("handsome"), or 「美女」 ("beautiful") if you're a woman. It isn't flirting, just a way of addressing people, so don't worry about it.
こんにちは！ このりんご、一斤いくらですか。: Hello! How much are these apples per jin?
中国の「一斤」は五百グラム。日本の「斤」（約六百グラム）とは違う、要注意の同形異: A Chinese 「一斤」 (jin) is 500 grams, a little over a pound. Price tags at markets and supermarkets are usually in 「元/斤」, so the price per kilogram is about twice what's shown.
一斤八元。甘いよ、ほら食べてみて。: Eight yuan a jin. They're very sweet. Here, try one.
うん、本当に甘い！ ちょっとまけてもらえますか。: Mm, they really are sweet! Could you make it a bit cheaper?
個人商店や市場では軽い値段交渉はよくあること。でも果物屋のように元々安い店で強く: Light bargaining is common at independent shops and markets. But haggling hard at a place like a fruit stand, where prices are low to begin with, is bad form. Keep it light, like 「可以便宜点儿吗？」, and if the answer is no, just smile and let it go.
もう十分安いのよ。たくさん買うならまけてあげる。: They're already really cheap. If you buy a lot, I can make it cheaper.
じゃあ三斤ください。それとスイカを半分。: Then I'll take three jin. And half a watermelon.
「买」mǎi（買う、第三声）と「卖」mài（売る、第四声）は声調だけの違い。逆に: 「买」 (「mǎi」, third tone, "to buy") and 「卖」 (「mài」, fourth tone, "to sell") differ only in tone. Mix them up and you say the exact opposite, so using 「我要」 ("I'd like") keeps you from making that mistake.
はいよ。りんご三斤で二十四、スイカが十五、合計三十九ね。端数はおまけして三十八で: OK! Three jin of apples is 24, the watermelon is 15, that's 39 altogether. I'll knock off the change, call it 38!
「抹零」は端数を切り捨ててくれること。店主の小さなサービスです。ここで「谢谢姐！: 「抹零」 means rounding down the odd amount, a small favor from the owner. If you reply 「谢谢姐！」 here, you'll instantly feel closer.
ありがとう、お姉さん！ アリペイで払えますか。: Thanks, sis! Can I pay with Alipay?
年上の女性店主には「姐」（お姉さん）、もっと年上なら「阿姨」（おばさん）と呼ぶと: Calling an older female shop owner 「姐」 ("big sister"), or 「阿姨」 ("auntie") if she's older still, sounds friendly. The trick is to address people as a bit younger than they actually are.
自分で金額を入力して払う方式のときは、支払い完了の画面を店主に見せるのがマナー。: When you pay by entering the amount yourself, it's good manners to show the owner your payment completed screen. Sometimes the owner's phone or speaker will announce 「支付宝到账三十八元」 ("Alipay received 38 yuan").
受け取ったよ。袋いる？: Got it. Do you want a bag?
一つください、ありがとうございます。僕、日本人で、中国語があまり上手じゃなくて。: One, please, thanks. I'm Japanese; my Chinese isn't very good.
上手じゃない！ また来てね！: Your Chinese is pretty good! Come again!
はい、また来ます。さようなら！: OK, I'll definitely come again. Bye!
中国の「一斤」は五百グラム。日本の斤とは違う。「两」は五十グラム: A Chinese 「一斤」 is 500 grams, a little over a pound. 「两」 is 50 grams
「多少钱一斤？」「这个多少钱？」。値段を聞く最重要フレーズ: 「多少钱一斤？」, 「这个多少钱？」. The most important phrase for asking prices
「八块」＝八元。「毛」は〇・一元。値札の「元」も口では「块」と読む: 「八块」 = eight yuan. 「毛」 is 0.1 yuan. 「元」 on price tags is also said as 「块」 in speech
「便宜点儿吧」＝まけて。日本語の「便宜」（都合）とは意味が違う: 「便宜点儿吧」 = make it cheaper. Note the reading 「pián yi」; the 「便」 in 「方便」 (convenient) is read 「biàn」
「太贵了！」は値段交渉の定番。背の高さの「高」とは区別する: 「太贵了！」 is a standard line in bargaining. Don't use 「高」, which means tall or high, for this
「尝尝」「尝一下」＝ちょっと食べてみて。市場では試食がよくある: 「尝尝」, 「尝一下」 = try a bit. Free tasting is common at markets
果物を褒める定番。「不甜不要钱！」（甘くなければお代はいらない）と言う店主も: The standard way to praise fruit. Some shop owners say 「不甜不要钱！」 ("If it's not sweet, it's free!")
「给你抹个零」＝端数はおまけするよ。個人商店ならではの心遣い: 「给你抹个零」 = I'll knock off the change for you. A courtesy typical of small independent shops
「付了」「付好了」＝払いました。「付钱」＝お金を払う: 「付了」, 「付好了」 = I've paid. 「付钱」 = to pay money
「要袋子吗？」＝袋いる？ スーパーでは有料で「塑料袋」と言う: 「要袋子吗？」 = Do you want a bag? At supermarkets you pay for them and call them 「塑料袋」
支払いやメッセージを受け取ったときの返事。「收到！」は「了解！」の意味でも使う: A reply when you've received a payment or message. 「收到！」 is also used to mean "Got it!"
「水果店」＝果物屋。「水果」はフルーツ全般: 「水果店」 = fruit shop. 「水果」 covers all kinds of fruit
夏の中国では半分や四分の一でも売ってくれる: In summer in China, they'll sell you even half or a quarter of one
……は一斤／一個いくら？: How much is... per jin / each?
もの + 多少钱 + 一 + 単位: item + 多少钱 + 一 + unit
量り売りや個数で売っているものの単価を聞く形。「这个多少钱？」だと全体の値段にな: A pattern for asking the unit price of things sold by weight or by the piece. 「这个多少钱？」 may get you the price for the whole lot, so at markets, saying the unit avoids misunderstandings. Asking prices isn't rude, so ask away.
このりんごは一斤いくら？: How much are these apples per jin?
肉まんは一個いくら？: How much are the steamed buns each?
この服はいくらですか。: How much is this piece of clothing?
少し安くしてもらえますか: Could you make it a bit cheaper?
可以 + 形容詞 + 一点儿 + 吗？: 可以 + adjective + 一点儿 + 「吗？」
「形容詞 + 一点儿」で「もう少し〜」と程度を和らげます。値段交渉の入口として使: "Adjective + 「一点儿」" softens the degree: "a bit more...." It's a phrase you can use to open bargaining, and adding 「可以……吗」 makes it a polite request. To push harder, try 「便宜点儿吧！」 with 「吧」.
少し安くしてもらえますか。: Could you make it a bit cheaper?
安くしてよ、二つ買うから。: Make it a bit cheaper, I'm buying two.
もう少しゆっくり話してもらえますか。: Could you speak a little more slowly?
ちょっと……してみる: to have a try at..., to... a little
一音節動詞を二回 / 動詞 + 一下: repeat a one-syllable verb / verb + 一下
「尝尝」「看看」のように動詞を重ねると「ちょっと〜してみて」という軽い感じになり: Doubling a verb, as in 「尝尝」 or 「看看」, gives a light feel: "have a little try." It softens a command, so shop owners and staff use it a lot. When you say it yourself, 「我看看」 ("I'm just looking") is a handy phrase when you're not sure whether to buy.
市場、果物屋、屋台など個人のお店。単価を聞く→試食→軽く交渉→スマホ決済、が一連: Markets, fruit stands, food stalls and other independent shops. Ask the unit price, taste, bargain lightly, pay by phone: that's the usual sequence. Chain stores and supermarkets have fixed prices, so you don't bargain there.
日本の「斤」のつもりで計算するとずれてしまいます。また、もともと安い店で何度もし: If you calculate as if a 「斤」 were a pound, your numbers will be off. Also, haggling persistently over and over at a shop where prices are already low, or complaining about prices marked on bags or signs, will put the owner in a bad mood. Bargain once, with a smile.
個人商店の店主にとって、毎日来てくれるお客さんは家族みたいなもの。外国人が中国語: For an independent shop owner, customers who come every day are like family. They're happy when a foreigner speaks to them in Chinese, so they'll knock off the change or throw in an extra one. That's their way of saying "Come again."
中国の町の小さな商店は、物を買うだけでなく、人と人がつながる場所です。最初は店主: Small neighborhood shops in China are not just places to buy things but places where people connect. You may be startled at first by how fast and loud the owners talk, but after a few visits they'll start chatting with you: "The watermelon's sweet today," "How were those apples the other day?" Paying by phone takes a second, but the exchange of 「谢谢姐」 and 「下次再来」 stays the same. You might be used to shopping quietly, but here people appreciate a little chat. A single line like 「你家的苹果最甜！」 ("Your apples are the sweetest!") reaches a shop owner's heart better than any perfect grammar.
中国の市場で「八块一斤」と書かれたりんご。一キロだといくら？: At a Chinese market, apples are marked 「八块一斤」. How much is a kilogram?
中国の一斤は五百グラム。一キロは二斤なので十六元です。日本の斤（約六百グラム）と: A Chinese jin is 500 grams. A kilogram is two jin, so it's 16 yuan. Don't confuse a jin with a pound.
「买」と「卖」の違いとして正しいのは？: Which correctly describes the difference between 「买」 and 「卖」?
買う(第三声)と売る(第四声): To buy (third tone) and to sell (fourth tone)
売る(第三声)と買う(第四声): To sell (third tone) and to buy (fourth tone)
買う mǎi は第三声、売る mài は第四声。声調を間違えると意味が逆になりま: "To buy," 「mǎi」, is third tone, and "to sell," 「mài」, is fourth tone. Get the tone wrong and the meaning is reversed.
店主に「给你抹个零」と言われました。どういう意味？: The shop owner says 「给你抹个零」. What does that mean?
端数をおまけする: The odd amount is knocked off.
「抹零」は端数を切り捨ててくれるサービス。「谢谢！」と笑顔で返しましょう。: 「抹零」 is a favor where the owner rounds down the odd amount. Reply with a smile and 「谢谢！」.
服屋で買うか迷っていて、ひとまず見るだけのときは？: You're in a clothing store, not sure whether to buy, and just want to look for now. What do you say?
「我看看」は「ちょっと見ているだけです」という柔らかい言い方。いきなり「我不买」: 「我看看」 is a soft way of saying "I'm just looking." Suddenly saying 「我不买」 ("I'm not buying") comes across as blunt.
